why: deletes overriding method(s) onRemove: whatever they did is gone -- port each to the new API, or say why vanilla no longer needs it
reviewed: Ported (CATALOG V48): 1.21.5 removed Block.onRemove; its drop half is vanilla's BlockEntity.preRemoveSideEffects, which drops any Container (this RandomizableContainerBlockEntity) only when the block changes, and its comparator update is now an affectNeighborsAfterRemoval override calling Containers.updateNeighboursAfterDestroy.

why: drops @Override from getStackForBone, getTransformTypeForStack and keeps the method: it then overrides nothing and never runs -- port it to the new signature, or delete it and say what vanilla now does instead
reviewed: Ported: GeckoLib 5 replaced getStackForBone/getTransformTypeForStack with getRelevantBones (RenderData per bone) and a renderStackForBone that takes the display context; both methods are now called from those overrides, reading the hand stacks captured in addRenderData, so the shield's NONE context still applies.

why: deletes overriding method(s) preRender: whatever they did is gone -- port each to the new API, or say why vanilla no longer needs it
reviewed: Ported: the preRender override (scale 1.0 for width and height) is back with GeckoLib 5's render-state signature.

reviewed: Ported as in 1.21.4: initializeClient is gone and Curios finds a curio renderer only through CuriosRendererRegistry; client/WingsThatCoverTheWorldClient registers WingsThatCoverTheWorldRenderer for the item at client setup.

why: drops @Override from canCraftInDimensions and keeps the method: it then overrides nothing and never runs -- port it to the new signature, or delete it and say what vanilla now does instead
reviewed: As in 1.21.4: canCraftInDimensions was removed from Recipe in 1.21.2 and nothing replaces it; its condition (grid at least 2x2) holds for every vanilla crafting grid, so the plain method changes nothing.

reviewed: Both handlers still apply with the same effect (checked against the 1.21.5 sources): Player no longer declares setItemSlot or drop(ItemStack, boolean, boolean) -- both are LivingEntity's now (CATALOG M30) -- so tls$blockSetItemSlot and tls$blockDrop are injected at HEAD of LivingEntity.setItemSlot / LivingEntity.drop(ItemStack,ZZ) in this target's LivingEntityMixin overlay, behind (Object) this instanceof Player with the same config switch, hasInventoryProtection and hasExternalCaller(5) checks; the call depth is unchanged (ServerPlayer.drop still overrides and calls super, as over Player in 1.21.1; no player class overrides setItemSlot).

why: empties 1 method body
reviewed: (inherited from 1.21.4) Stale: raised against the pre-1.1.2 overlay. The overlay now carries the authors' 1.1.2 TestEntity (spawn position, healthManagementReady) and differs from it only by the 1.21.4 signatures (customServerAiStep/kill/dropExperience take a ServerLevel, canTeleport); its empty bodies (checkDespawn, doPush, pushEntities, knockback, init) are the authors' own, and the current overlay no longer raises this signal.
